frozen_problem.title: Tate-completion obstruction and finite torsion windows for the motivic filtration on TC of the sphere
frozen_problem.statement:
The motivic filtration on the algebraic $K$-theory of the sphere spectrum

Due to work of Rognes, Blumberg--Mandell, and others, we understand the algebraic K-theory of the sphere spectrum fairly well. Recent work of Hahn--Raksit--Wilson \cite{arXiv:2206.11208} gives a motivic filtration on TC of $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-rings which is closely related to the motivic filtration on algebraic K-theory in motivic homotopy theory.

Can one understand the motivic filtration (or motivic spectral sequence) on the $\mathrm{TC}$ of the sphere spectrum? What about for the motivic filtration on related invariants such as $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TP}$?

theory.target: Audit the uniform-annihilator prerequisite for commuting rationalization with an inverse limit, using reduction towers Z/p^n and a bounded-exponent control; no computation of sphere TC or Tate spectra.
definitions: A_n=Z/p^n with reduction maps; A consists of compatible sequences.
Rationalization is localization at nonzero integers.
A common annihilator is one integer killing every coordinate; stagewise annihilators may vary.
assumptions: All experimental objects are ordinary abelian groups, not spectra or filtered TC.
Tower transition is reduction modulo p^(n-1); level zero is the trivial group.
The ordinary infinite argument uses localization at nonzero integers and compatibility of all coordinates; it is not inferred from finite tests.
approaches_considered: Direct finite-group addition and exhaustive compatible paths.
Stagewise rationalization shortcut, retired without an extra continuity theorem.
falsification_targets: Nonzero integer killing every unit coordinate.
Incorrect residue orders, fiber counts or bounded-exponent control.

claims.statement: The two implementations agree on 32 finite groups comprising 4008 elements, 480 denominator escapes and 52 exponent escapes.
claims.falsification_condition: An incorrect additive order, residue, reduction fiber, path or omitted parameter.

claims.statement: The ordinary compatible-unit argument gives a counterexample to commuting rationalization with inverse limit for Z/p^n. This universal argument is not independently authored or kernel verified.
claims.falsification_condition: A nonzero integer annihilating the entire unit sequence, an incompatible unit sequence, or a misapplication of module localization.

claims.statement: A common nonzero annihilator suffices to make the rationalization of an ordinary inverse limit vanish; this condition holds for the capped-exponent control. Not a general spectral continuity theorem.
claims.falsification_condition: Failure of coordinatewise action or common annihilator in the specified control.

claims.statement: Finite-stage rational vanishing alone does not supply the single annihilator needed for an element of the limit; the imported Tate and motivic claims need separate spectral comparison and convergence arguments.
claims.falsification_condition: A justified comparison theorem supplying the missing hypotheses for the intended spectral objects.

claims.statement: Stacks 00CM gives the localization relation; HRW v3 abstract includes the sphere; Burklund-Subramanian v1 Theorem 1.1 states the p-complete sphere Tate equivalence. AIM page unavailable. No TC calculation is verified by these citations.
claims.falsification_condition: Wrong source version, missing hypotheses or a claim not located in the cited source.
